hook: Walking Canada's coastline would take you more than 27 years.

beats.narration: Walking Canada's coastline would take you more than 27 years.
beats.claim: 202,080 km at 20 km per day is about 27.7 years.

beats.narration: It's 202,080 kilometres long. The longest coastline on Earth.
beats.claim: Canada's coastline is 202,080 km per the CIA World Factbook, the longest in the world.

beats.narration: The reason is up north. The Canadian Arctic Archipelago has 36,563 islands, each with its own shore.
beats.claim: The Canadian Arctic Archipelago consists of 36,563 islands.

beats.narration: But measure with a finer ruler, and the same coast becomes 265,523 kilometres.
beats.claim: The World Resources Institute gives Canada's coastline as 265,523 km.

beats.narration: Zoom in, and a coastline keeps getting longer. It's called the coastline paradox.
beats.claim: The coastline paradox explains why the World Factbook and WRI report different lengths for Canada.

beats.narration: So Canada's coastline has no true length. Only the length of your ruler.

title: Walking Canada's coastline would take 27 years
description: Canada has the longest coastline on Earth. But how long is it really? Depends on your ruler.
